name: Greece
tagline: About twenty English-taught degrees, and a Greek-taught route that needs B2 Greek
ownCitizens: If you hold Greek citizenship, the parts of this page written for other EU/EEA citizens — registering your right of residence, proving your fee status — are not about you, and Greece's own student grants and loans are open to you on their ordinary terms; check them, because some depend on where you have lived. Your IB is still a foreign qualification here, so the IB entry rules on this page still apply to you.
summary: Greek public universities teach almost entirely in Greek. There are two ways in for an IB student at a school in Denmark. The first is one of about twenty English-taught bachelor's at public universities, applied for directly on the IB, which charge €4,500–€17,000 a year. The second is a Greek-taught place through the ministry's eight-day July window for graduates of foreign schools, which needs B2 Greek before you can enrol. Private colleges such as ACG teach in English and award US- or UK-validated degrees.
whyConsider: The English-taught programmes take the IB directly. There are no Panhellenic exams.
As an EU citizen you need no visa, and there is a ministry route into Greek-taught public places for graduates of EU schools.
watchOuts: The ministry window is eight days long and fell on 2 to 9 July in 2026, the week IB results come out. Have every document translated into Greek by June.
A Greek-taught place cannot be taken up without a B2 Greek certificate. Without it you enrol a year later or lose the place.
Check that the programme itself is taught in English. A university with an English website may still have no English-taught bachelor programmes.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: Set per programme. There is no national minimum for the English-taught programmes.
notes: On the ministry route the IB counts as a foreign school-leaving qualification under category B1 (EU-member-state schools).

language.englishTaughtBachelors: About twenty fee-paying programmes at ten public universities (September 2026), led by Aristotle University, Athens and AUEB, plus English-taught Medicine at five universities and the private colleges.
notes: Greek-taught places through the ministry route need a B2 Greek certificate to enrol.

feeContext.summary: English-taught public programmes charge the same tuition to EU and non-EU students: from €4,500 a year (Aegean) to €8,000 for most bachelor's, and €12,000–€17,000 for Medicine — €17,000 at Athens in 2026-27, €6,000 for its BA in Ancient Greece. Fees on Greek-taught places are not confirmed here.

sectorLandscape.summary: All Greek universities (ΑΕΙ, πανεπιστήμια) are state institutions. The technological institutes (ΤΕΙ) have been merged into them. A few other public academies sit beside the universities. Private colleges (κολλέγια) teach foreign universities' degrees, and since law 5094/2024 foreign universities may open non-state branches.

routes.what: Every public university, from Athens and Thessaloniki to Crete and the Aegean. Mostly taught in Greek. Entry is by Panhellenic exams for Greek schools, by the ministry's foreign-nationals route for foreign school graduates, or by direct application to the few English-taught programmes.

Public institutions outside the universities: teacher training for vocational education (ΑΣΠΑΙΤΕ), tourism education (ΑΣΤΕ), and the ecclesiastical academies. The ministry's foreign-nationals circular is addressed to them alongside the universities.
routes.note: On the same ministry route; not covered further on this site.

routes.what: Private, fee-paying, taught in English, awarding a foreign partner's or US-accredited degree rather than a Greek state degree. The American College of Greece (Deree) is one.

Non-profit branches of foreign universities, licensed under law 5094/2024. The ministry re-issued licences to the Keele and York branches in August 2026 after Council of State rulings annulled the first ones.
routes.note: New, and still being argued in the courts. What these branches offer to a 2027 applicant is not covered here.

jurisdictions.name: Public universities
jurisdictions.summary: Greek-taught places through the ministry's July window, which needs B2 Greek to enrol, or English-taught programmes applied for directly.

jurisdictions.name: Private colleges
jurisdictions.summary: Apply to the college. Degrees are validated or accredited abroad.
